ai_summary: Great Britain's wind fleet is currently generating 13.2 GW, with estimated Scottish wind output providing 4.9 GW, which represents 48.5% of installed Scottish wind capacity. This robust renewable performance has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to an exceptional 0 gCO2/kWh, standing in stark contrast to the GB-wide carbon intensity of 121 gCO2/kWh. However, persistent cross-border transmission constraints continue to prevent this surplus clean energy from reaching southern demand centres. As a direct result, Scottish generation curtailed so far today has reached 48.9 GWh through Balancing Mechanism bids, accumulating a constraint cost of about £1,250,906. To replace this lost zero-carbon power, thermal plants had to ramp up elsewhere on the network, leading to an estimated 9,288,302 m3 of gas burned elsewhere and producing an avoidable 17,110 tonnes of CO2. Extrapolating this daily constraint expense across a full year indicates an estimated total yearly cost of curtailment of approximately £457 million. This operational bottleneck places a direct, unnecessary financial burden on consumers, adding an estimated £1.60/MWh to everybody's invoice in the UK while undermining national carbon reduction objectives.
